headline: Chips and AI Hardware Lead a Split Session as Homebuilders Slump
body_html:
Wednesday's session ended in a near stalemate on the surface: 276 of the 538 stocks we track rose and 256 fell. Underneath, the money was clearly choosy. Semiconductors were the strongest group, up 1.56%, and the AI-hardware supply chain did most of the heavy lifting. Vertiv Holdings climbed 16.48%, Flex gained 11.61%, Forgent Power Solutions rose 8.45% and Sandisk added 7.66%. A market chatter item about Micron's big rally fit the same story.

Healthcare was the other bright spot, up 0.88%. Genmab was the standout mover of the day, surging 28.25%, and Ensign Group added 8.62%. Consumer, materials and energy finished almost flat. The weakness was concentrated in Homebuilders, down 1.48%, followed by Software at 0.64% lower and Industrials at 0.56% lower. Single-stock damage was sharp: F5 fell 20.43%, Landstar System 17.76%, Enphase Energy 16.03% and CoStar Group 13.96%.

The market's tone also reflects a Federal Reserve chairman sounding firm on inflation while policy sits on pause. Rate-sensitive homebuilders finishing last is consistent with that, though we would not read too much into one day. Thursday, October 29, brings the next test of whether the chip-led leadership can hold.

briefs.headline: Genmab Rockets Higher on a Banner Day for Biotech
briefs.body: Genmab was the session's top performer in our universe, jumping 28.25%. That helped push Healthcare up 0.88% as a group. Ensign Group, a post-acute care provider, also did well, rising 8.62%.

briefs.headline: Memory and Electronics Makers Ride the Chip Rally
briefs.body: Sandisk rose 7.66% and Flex gained 11.61% as Semiconductors climbed 1.56%, the best showing among our sectors. Commentary circulating today pointed to a strong rally at Micron, reinforcing the sense that memory demand is back in focus.

briefs.headline: Data-Center Power Gear Surges, but One Big Name Slips
briefs.body: Vertiv Holdings leapt 16.48% and Forgent Power Solutions advanced 8.45%, both tied to power and cooling for data centers. Meanwhile, GE Vernova shares reportedly dipped even after a beat-and-raise quarter, a sign of how selective buyers were.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Lag as the Fed Keeps Its Hawkish Tone
briefs.body: Homebuilders were the weakest group, down 1.48%. The Fed chairman struck a firm stance on inflation, and commentary around the central bank's rate pause suggests borrowing costs may stay elevated, which is a headwind for housing.

briefs.headline: Refiners Shine While Fuel Costs Bite Elsewhere
briefs.body: Phillips 66 reported a record quarterly profit on strong refining results. Energy stocks were nearly flat, down 0.08%. Elsewhere, reports of cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia after a jump in fuel prices showed the cost side of that trade.

briefs.headline: Sharp Single-Stock Drops Hit Software, Freight and Solar
briefs.body: F5 sank 20.43%, Landstar System fell 17.76%, Enphase Energy lost 16.03% and CoStar Group dropped 13.96%. The declines were spread across very different industries, and Software as a group slipped 0.64%.
